title: Separating parameters and the bad-parameter subfield of a smooth curve
statement: Let $K$ be a separably closed field [def-kun-separably-closed] and $L/K$ a finitely generated extension of transcendence degree one [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. Assume $L$ is the function field of a smooth integral finite-type $K$-scheme of dimension one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The function field is the local ring at the generic point. Every $x\in L$ transcendental over $K$ makes $L/K(x)$ finite. There exists such an $x$ with $L/K(x)$ separable [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. In characteristic $p>0$, let $D=KL^p$ be the smallest subfield of $L$ containing $K$ and all $p$th powers from $L$; in characteristic zero put $D=K$. Then $D$ is a proper $K$-linear subspace of $L$, and for every $x\in L$, $x\notin D$ if and only if $x$ is transcendental over $K$ and $L/K(x)$ is finite separable.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 2.1.8, printed p. 13, separating-transcendence-basis paragraph; smoothness-to-separability also Stacks Tag 037X, algebra-lemma-localization-smooth-separable; the characteristic-p criterion is the separating-parameter criterion quoted in that paragraph.

proof.text: Fix $x\in L$ transcendental over $K$, and put $F=K(x)$. The singleton $\{x\}$ is a transcendence basis of $F/K$, so $\operatorname{trdeg}_K F=1$. The tower formula gives $1=1+\operatorname{trdeg}_F L$, hence $\operatorname{trdeg}_F L=0$ and $L/F$ is algebraic. Choose the given finite field-generating family $L=K(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$. Then $L=F(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$, and each $a_i$ is algebraic over $F$. The algebraic-generators theorem gives $[L:F]<\infty$. This establishes the first assertion without using separability.

Let $C$ be the smooth integral $K$-scheme in the hypotheses, so its structure morphism $C\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is smooth. Choose a nonempty affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq C$. The inclusion is an open immersion, so by [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition] the composite $\operatorname{Spec}A\to C\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is smooth; it is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the structure map $K\to A$, so [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] makes $K\to A$ a smooth ring map in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. Integrality makes $A$ a domain, and the generic-point fraction-field identification identifies its fraction field, compatibly over $K$, with $L$. Apply [lem-trf-smooth-domain-fraction-separably-generated] to this $A$ and $L$. Thus $L/K$ is separable in the nonalgebraic sense; no perfection of $K$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 037X, lemma-localization-smooth-separable; affine-local smoothness as in 01V4; generic fraction-field identification as in 01RV.

proof.text: Apply the definition of a separable field extension to the finitely generated intermediate field $L$ itself. It gives a separating transcendence basis. Its cardinality is $\operatorname{trdeg}_K L=1$, so it consists of one element $t$. Then $t$ is transcendental and $L/K(t)$ is separable algebraic; step 1 makes it finite. This proves existence. The separating-basis differential theorem says that $dt$ is an $L$-basis of $\Omega_{L/K}$, which therefore has dimension one and is nonzero. Here and below $d$ denotes the universal $K$-derivation.

proof.text:
For every $x\in L$, put $F=K(x)$. The first differential exact sequence identifies $\Omega_{L/F}$ with the quotient of $\Omega_{L/K}$ by the image of $L\otimes_F\Omega_{F/K}$. That image is precisely $L\,dx$: $x\in F$, and every $f\in F$ is $P(x)/Q(x)$ with $Q(x)
e0$, so the derivation rules give $df=(P\prime(x)Q(x)-P(x)Q\prime(x))Q(x)^{-2}dx$. If $dx
e0$, this line is all of the one-dimensional space in step 3. Thus $\Omega_{L/F}=0$. The same finite generators as over $K$ generate $L/F$, so [lem-weil-pbc-fg-field-zero-differentials-separable] implies $L/F$ finite separable. The tower formula then gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_K F=1$, so $x$ cannot be algebraic over $K$ (an algebraic $K(x)/K$ has degree of transcendence zero). Conversely, if $x$ is transcendental and $L/F$ finite separable, the polynomial differential basis theorem for $K[X]$ and its localization to $F=K(x)$ make $dx$ an $F$-basis of $\Omega_{F/K}$. Finite-separable differential base change sends $1\otimes dx$ to $dx$ and is an isomorphism onto $\Omega_{L/K}$. Consequently $dx
e0$. We have proved $dx
e0$ if and only if $x$ is transcendental and $L/K(x)$ is finite separable.

proof.text: Assume $\operatorname{char}K=0$. We claim that every $x\in L$ algebraic over $K$ belongs to $K$. Indeed $F=K(x)$ is finitely generated and algebraic over $K$, so its transcendence degree is zero. The characteristic-zero separability theorem and the definition of nonalgebraic separability applied to $F$ give a separating transcendence basis with zero elements. Thus $F/K$ is separable algebraic, and it is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-generators-finite-extension]. Separably closedness of $K$ forces $F=K$. Consequently $x\notin K$ if and only if $x$ is transcendental over $K$. For such $x$, step 1 gives $L/K(x)$ finite. Apply the characteristic-zero theorem with base $K(x)$; since $L/K(x)$ is algebraic its separating basis is empty, so the extension is separable algebraic. Conversely, a transcendental $x$ is outside $K$ by definition. This is exactly the required criterion for $D=K$. The subfield $K$ is a $K$-linear subspace and is proper because the element $t$ of step 3 is transcendental.
